title: Le Chatelier's Principle Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
Squeeze into a crowded bus and everyone shuffles to make room. Open a fizzy drink and gas rushes out. Push on something balanced, and it pushes back. In this animated lesson for Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 6, Equilibrium) Diya opens a pressure cooker and we learn to predict what any push does to an equilibrium.

You will see Le Chatelier's rule on a see-saw, then add hydrogen to H2 + I2 = 2HI on the molecule bench and watch Q fall below K and climb back. A piston shows why squeezing favours the side with fewer gas molecules, proved step by step for CO + 3H2 = CH4 + H2O (Q becomes K/4). We test an inert gas at constant volume, temperature (it changes K), and a catalyst (no shift, equilibrium sooner), compare brown NO2 in ice and hot water (Delta H = -57.2 kJ/mol), and walk through the Haber process (Delta H = -92.38 kJ/mol, about 500 C and 200 atm, iron catalyst, as in NCERT). Then a worked example with Kc = 57.0 (Q = 28.5 after adding hydrogen), the exam trap, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 64 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.
